note: One continuing investigation rather than six separate questions (`FOLLOWUPS.md` item 39): a `0x9F DRIVER_POWER_STATE_FAILURE` walked from the bug check to the driver holding the IRP, the walk `docs/crash-dump-walkthrough.md` sections 2 and 4 do by hand. Every step after the first depends on the one before it - the IRP comes from the bug check's fourth parameter, the operation and the device from that IRP's current stack location, the driver from that device - so a wrong turn at step 2 leaves steps 3 to 8 with nothing to read, and per-task grading would score that as six failures. `--scenario` grades it as a run instead: the facts below in order, the step at which each was first stated (searched from the step that asks for it onward, never before - an earlier answer can carry a fact by accident, and `0x9F_3_ACPI_IMAGE_pci.sys` is a failure bucket containing `acpi`), and the first fact never stated, which is where the run stopped being recoverable. Run it with `WINDBG_MCP_SCENARIO` set, which the runner does for any suite carrying `facts`. Steps 8 and 9 are what make it an investigation the *transcript* can fill: each needs the whole module table, which `modules` answers 32 rows at a time by default, so a model that gets there has asked for all 227 rows and the driver has handed it the whole result - text and structured content together - on top of everything before it. `v1` was the first seven steps, whose results are all small: run once on 2026-10-17, every cell held every fact with the transcript never more than 31,130 tokens, which measured the surface rather than the investigation. Two traps are deliberate. `!analyze` blames `pci` on a host with `triage\triage.ini` beside the engine (bucket `0x9F_3_ACPI_IMAGE_pci.sys`, read 2026-10-17) - the bus driver, not the one holding the IRP - so a model that takes its word at step 5 goes wrong, and step 6 then asks where the wrong driver is loaded. And the IRP has two power stack locations, `IRP_MN_WAIT_WAKE` on the PDO and `IRP_MN_SET_POWER` at the current one, so reading the wrong location answers step 3 with the wrong minor function. Every fact was read through this server's own read-only tools on 2026-10-17 and each carries a `verify` binding, so `--verify-key` re-takes this key as it does the suite's. `possible_on` is a prediction and too pessimistic in one direction (`.claude/skills/eval-bench/SKILL.md`): steps 3 to 8 are marked `full` because `irp_stack` and `device_object` are in the `ioctl` group and step 8 starts from the driver they find, but a `lean` client is served `read_memory` and could in principle walk `_IRP` and `_DEVICE_OBJECT` by hand.

facts.note: `driver_power_statefailure` is not a typo. An alternative is matched against the answer after `normalise()`, which strips `_`, `'` and a backtick between two hex digits so that an address WinDbg splits in two reads as one - and `E_F` in `STATE_FAILURE` is two hex digits. So every spelling of the name a model or the server writes with underscores arrives here as `driver_power_statefailure`, and the natural `driver_power_state_failure` would have marked every correct answer wrong. Found by `test_the_shipped_scenario_agrees_with_its_own_bindings` before any run.

The table `modules` answers is sorted by start address (all 227 rows, checked 2026-10-17), so the pins at indices 151 and 152 are the relation itself: `nvlddmkm` ends at 0xfffff80338eab000 and the next image to start is `fastfat`, at 0xfffff80338eb0000.

Ranked from all 227 rows on 2026-10-17: `nvlddmkm` 112,766,976 B, `igdkmd64` 44,216,320, `nt` 21,299,200, no tie at second. The pins hold the three sizes; that no other row falls between the first two is the ranking, which a pin cannot state and the 2026-10-17 read did.
